Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Request — bespoke SLO, routing fallback & commercial ask

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Orbit's engineering and compliance teams are leaning towards Redwood, but we need to align on one outstanding piece before we commit: our regulated workload requires a slightly different SLA and a routing fallback for critical windows. High level ask below:

- Reduce the uptime target in the standard SLO to 99.90% for the first 12 months of the pilot (currently 99.95%).
- Cap cumulative service credits to 25% of the monthly invoice (we need predictability on commercial exposure).
- Authorize a routing policy that allows Redwood to fall back to the auxiliary model pool (quantized/variant models) for short bursts to preserve availability; Orbit will accept the functional trade-off during fallbacks.
- We'd like a 12-month term and an introductory commercial concession (we're targeting enterprise volume in year 2).

I've attached a short proposal that shows our risk tolerance and proposed credit cap. Can you route this to deal desk / leadership for an exec decision? We'll need this in place before procurement signs the PO.

Best,
Aiden Porter
VP, Platform Engineering
Orbit Technologies

Aiden — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the proposal. I copied Marissa (deal desk) and Ben (sales lead) to triage commercial/legal constraints. Quick notes from my side:

- Technical: Routing to the auxiliary model pool is feasible as a short-term fallback; we should define a max window (e.g., 10 minutes per incident) and monitoring/rollback criteria so Orbit can signal if fallback materially impacts outputs.
- Commercial: The credit cap you proposed (25% of monthly invoice) is within the realm of what we've approved for similar pilots, but will require exec signoff on discount and term.
- Timing: Procurement is asking for final language by next Friday to keep the Q3 kickoff.

Marissa / Ben — can you review Aiden's attachment and propose a commercial + SLO amendment we can present to execs? Please include: 1) recommended discount for 12-month commit, 2) precise SLO wording we can add to the MSA, 3) any region or routing constraints. Lauren from legal is on copy in case we need redlines.

I'll coordinate with Orbit on rollout cadence and monitoring requirements once we have the commercial guardrails.

— Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:23:47 -0700
Subject: Deal desk proposal — Orbit (DL-2027-0891) SLO & commercial recommendation

Team — I reviewed Orbit's proposal and sketched a commercially conservative amendment that balances Orbit's needs with Redwood's risk:

Proposed commercial package:
- Term: 12 months (auto-renew) with a 30-day termination right during pilot phase.
- Intro discount: 18% off list for the first 12 months (reflects pilot commitment + volume ramp).
- Service credit cap: 25% of monthly invoice per calendar month (matches Orbit ask).

SLO amendment (draft language for MSA):
- Standard uptime target shall be amended to 99.90% for the initial 12-month period for services supporting Orbit's regulated workload.
- Service credits for uptime deviations will be applied per the schedule in Appendix A, with total credit liability capped at 25% of the monthly invoice.
- Redwood is permitted to route requests to auxiliary model variants or alternative regional pools for up to 10 continuous minutes per incident and up to 60 minutes total per calendar month for the affected service. Redwood must notify Orbit via the incident channel and include a remediation plan.

Operational/controls ask:
- Redwood must provide a dedicated monitoring dashboard for the Orbit scope and enable an alerting hook to Orbit's PagerDuty.
- Automatic rollback clause: if fallbacks are associated with an accuracy regression >5% against a pre-agreed prompt set, Redwood will revert to primary model routing and engage the joint ops cadence.

Attachments: Redwood_SLO_Redline_v1.docx (redlined amendment)

Risk notes: this reduces our SLO obligation and limits credit exposure to a known cap. The routing allowance increases availability but introduces variability in output quality — the automatic rollback clause is intended to protect Orbit's correctness requirements.

Request: Exec signoff required on the discount (18%) and the routing allowance. Legal (Lauren) — please confirm the redline is acceptable or flag material risk.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Orbit DL-2027-0891 — recommendation to approve

Marissa / Hannah — quick endorsement. Orbit is strategically important (large product integration later this year) and the commercial terms are reasonable for a pilot. A few operational guardrails I want called out for execs:

- Limit the routing allowance to US regions for the first 90 days (minimizes multi-region blast radius).
- Require a joint 2-week canary in production with focused quality evaluation before any full cutover.
- Tie the 18% discount to usage tiers (graduated rollback to list pricing if usage doesn't hit the agreed ramp in months 6/9).

If Jonas is comfortable with the commercial exposure and the limited regional scope, I'd approve.

— Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Orbit DL-2027-0891 — executive signoff

Approve as proposed with the clarifications below. Rationale: strategic placement in our ecosystem and clear operational mitigations make the exposure manageable. Approvals:

- Commercial: approve 18% introductory discount for 12 months. Discount will be tiered and subject to the usage ramp milestones in the deal desk addendum (Marissa, please draft gating language for months 6 & 9).
- SLO amendment: approve temporary SLO of 99.90% for 12 months with service credit cap of 25% of monthly invoice.
- Routing: approve auxiliary model pool routing for up to 10 minutes per incident and up to 60 minutes per month, limited to US region for the first 90 days.
- Operational requirements before full rollout: 2-week canary, dedicated monitoring dashboard, PagerDuty integration, and an agreed prompt set for quality evaluation. If accuracy regression >5% during canary, Redwood will pause routing fallbacks and remediate.

Action items:
1) Marissa — finalize amendment language and the tiered discount gating; include monitoring SLIs that Orbit will access.
2) Lauren — prepare MSA amendment and schedule a 1-hour review with Orbit legal next week.
3) Hannah — inform Orbit procurement and confirm the PO timing; set up the canary ops calendar.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
